name: GPIO Restriction Warner
blurb: risks of using boot straps and special-purpose GPIOs
intro: Lists the pins of a chip that are boot straps, wired to flash or PSRAM, input only, used for debug, USB or the serial bootloader, or limited in drive or voltage, and flags the ones among the pins you plan to use. Severity high means a wrong level at reset can stop the chip from booting or being programmed. Data from the chips' datasheets.

inputs.label: Pins you plan to use
inputs.placeholder: GPIO numbers (12, IO12) or names (PA13, PB6)

inputs.label: Module has PSRAM or octal flash
On a Raspberry Pi Pico board

examples.title: ESP32 sensor board with an analog input on GPIO4 and Wi-Fi
Blue Pill using SWD pins and PC13

input.pins: PA13, PB3, PC13, PA9, PA10, PA2

usage: Give the chip (esp32, esp32s3, esp32c3, esp8266, stm32f103, rp2040, atmega328p) and the pins you plan to use as a comma list (GPIO numbers for ESP/RP2040, names like PA13 for STM32/AVR); set wifi, psram and board for the conditional limits. It returns counts of high/medium risks, your restricted pins with what to do, the full special-pin table, and a warning for every high-severity pin (boot straps, flash pins, SWD). Use it while choosing pins for a schematic or firmware.
sources: Espressif ESP32 datasheet §2.4 strapping pins; ESP32-WROOM-32E / WROVER-E datasheets
